title: Coefficient ideal intersection for a split symmetric presentation
statement: Let $P$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq P$ an ideal, $A=P/I$, and $M=I/I^2$ projective over $A$. Let $m\geq0$ and let $q:A^m\to M$ be surjective. Put $C=\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. Let $\alpha:A[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\to C$ be an $A$-algebra map with $\alpha(y_j)=\iota(q(e_j))$, and let $\varphi:P[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\to C$ equal its composite with coefficient reduction $\pi$. Put $H=\ker\pi$ and $J=\ker\varphi$. Then $H\cap J^2=HJ$. The zero quotient ring and the empty variable set are allowed.

proof.text: Split q by the Mathlib projective lifting theorem. Send the standard basis to polynomial variables by k. The hypothesis on α gives αk = ιq. Extend ks using SymmetricAlgebra.lift to σ; generator extensionality and qs = id show ασ = id.

Coefficient reduction π is surjective. Lift each σ(α(y_j)) to Q and substitute these lifts to construct β, fixing coefficient constants. Polynomial generator extensionality gives πβ = σαπ and thus φβ = φ. Therefore β(J) ⊆ H, H ⊆ J, and β(x)-x ∈ J for all x. All witness choices here use proved Mathlib surjectivity, not unproved existence.

If x ∈ H, coeff_map shows each coefficient constant belongs to H. Expand x with MvPolynomial.as_sum. Since β fixes constants, each summand of β(x)-x is a coefficient in H times a monomial difference in J. Therefore β(x)-x ∈ HJ.

For x ∈ H ∩ J², map_pow and β(J) ⊆ H imply β(x) ∈ H² ⊆ HJ. Subtract the difference β(x)-x ∈ HJ to get x ∈ HJ. The reverse inclusion is ideal multiplication monotonicity using H ⊆ J. The zero quotient and empty variable cases require no separate assumptions.

proof_origin.note: Direct algebraic proof using the projective splitting and polynomial substitution; replaces the local regular sequence route below the unit level. No new unproved statements.

theorem projective_symmetric_coefficient_intersection
    (P : Type u) [CommRing P] (I : Ideal P) (m : ℕ)
    [Module.Projective (P ⧸ I) I.Cotangent]
    (q : (Fin m → P ⧸ I) →ₗ[P ⧸ I] I.Cotangent) (hq : Function.Surjective q)
    (α : MvPolynomial (Fin m) (P ⧸ I) →ₐ[P ⧸ I] SymmetricAlgebra (P ⧸ I) I.Cotangent)
    (hαX : ∀ j, α (MvPolynomial.X j) =
      SymmetricAlgebra.ι (P ⧸ I) I.Cotangent (q (Pi.single j 1)))
    (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) P →+* SymmetricAlgebra (P ⧸ I) I.Cotangent)
    (hφeq : φ = α.toRingHom.comp (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) :
    RingHom.ker (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (σ := Fin m)) ⊓
        (RingHom.ker φ) ^ 2 =
      RingHom.ker (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (σ := Fin m)) *
        RingHom.ker φ
